Bilateral elbow contractures restricted passive range of motion (ROM) of 20-150 degrees, and gastrosoleus contractures impacted ankles, limiting passive ankle ROM of 40-50 degrees of plantar flexion (Figure 2). Depressed deep tendon reflexes in both upper and lower limbs were noted, while sensory examination yielded unremarkable findings. in_text_mentions: Further assessment at a higher medical center in September 2023 included an MRI of her lower limbs, unveiling moderate fatty infiltration in bilateral thighs with relative sparing of bilateral gracilis, sartorius, and rectus femoris muscles. Severe fatty replacement manifested in bilateral soleus muscles (Figure 1). Referral to the Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PMR) department for further management and rehabilitation followed.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A1, A2, A3, A4, B1, B2). A1: Axial thigh MRI from the EDMD proband showing bilateral thigh muscle disappearance with extensive adipose replacement, a radiological manifestation of the muscular dystrophy. A2: Second axial thigh MRI slice from the EDMD proband confirming bilateral thigh muscle disappearance filled with adipose tissue. A3: Axial calf MRI from the EDMD proband showing mild fatty infiltration of the anteromedial calf muscle group, matching the configured calf fatty infiltration finding. A4: Second axial calf MRI slice from the EDMD proband confirming mild fatty infiltration of the anteromedial calf muscles. B1: H&E histology from the EDMD proband showing dystrophic muscle changes: variation in fiber size with alternating atrophy and hypertrophy, and fat/connective tissue proliferation. B2: MGT histology from the EDMD proband showing split muscle fibers within hypertrophic fibers, a dystrophic pathological change.

in_text_mentions: A Cardiology consultation was obtained. Coronary angiography demonstrated a left-dominant coronary circulation without significant stenoses or atherosclerotic lesions. Cardiac MRI corroborated the findings of dilated cardiomyopathy, showing global hypokinesia and an LVEF of 35%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging revealed moderate myocardial fibrosis in a mixed pattern, involving both ischemic (subendocardial) and non-ischemic (mid-wall) regions, particularly in the lateral wall (Figure 4), suggestive of a genetic cardiomyopathy.

A: Cardiac MRI cine frame of the EDMD patient (disease-focused article title) showing the captioned manifestation of a slightly dilated left ventricle (EDVi 98 mL/m2, EDV 220 mL) with systolic function at the lower limit of normal (LVEF 58%); no vocabulary finding key covers cardiac involvement, so terms are proposed. DCM is a recognized but less classic cardiac feature of EDMD (typically AV block/atrial cardiomyopathy), hence variant with moderate confidence. B: Systolic 2-chamber cine image of the same EDMD patient documenting the captioned LV dilatation with borderline systolic function (ESV 92 mL, LVEF 58%). C: 4-chamber diastolic MRI view showing the slightly dilated LV confirmed in the caption as dilated cardiomyopathy in this EDMD patient. D: 4-chamber systolic cine frame documenting LV volumes/ejection fraction in the EDMD patient with confirmed dilated cardiomyopathy. E: Short-axis diastolic MRI view of the EDMD patient's...

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Shows a child exhibiting clinical presentation consistent with muscle dystrophy, consistent with the article context of weakness in a young patient. B: Direct visualization of a characteristic flexion contracture and muscle wasting involving the upper limb. C: Shows muscle wasting in the trunk/hip area which corresponds to the clinical description of weakness in the cervical, lumbar, and pelvic muscles. D: Shows lower limb involvement including wasting and ankle deformity, characteristic of the disease.
